findings: The pinned parity polynomial equals the truncated Newton interpolant at all coefficients because both have degree below R and agree at the R defining nodes.
Integer upper-translation matrices satisfy T(a)T(b)=T(a+b), so T(-A) is an exact inverse of the native T(A).
Every native parity coefficient is T(-A) applied to the exact vector (-1)^A(-2)^j.
An independent exact solver matched the formula in 324 cases and detected positive-shift, missing-parity-sign, and dropped-last-term mutants.
